title: A recommender that records why it recommended
status: Design complete and reviewed. Data work begins with Milestone 2, once groups are assigned on October 19.

overview.question: Can a carefully tuned, leakage-safe pipeline predict the next rating a user submits on MovieLens 1M better than a well-tuned simple baseline, and can it show that with honest intervals?
overview.summary: Every phase is fixed before any result is seen: the split, the baselines, the tuning budget and the conclusion's possible verdicts. Twelve predictive models climb from simple linear regression to stacking, each judged against a regularised bias model under the same budget, with uncertainty clustered by user.

The value of the next rating a user submits — never a film watched
Twelve models and ten supporting techniques

scope.principle: The timestamps record when a rating was submitted, not when a film was watched. Every question, feature and metric concerns rating submissions.

phases.title: Scope, fixed before anything runs
points: Question, unit and target declared in writing before any code.
Target: rating in {1..5}, ordinal, modelled as continuous — recorded as a limitation, not hidden.
Metrics: RMSE, MAE, and the macro-averaged MAEM and RMSEM, which an imbalanced ordinal target requires.
Predictions left unrounded, so figures stay comparable with published work.

phases.title: Structural audit (all rows)
points: Load with latin-1; movies.dat is not UTF-8.
Shape, types, duplicates, target sanity, referential integrity.
Distinguish 3,706 films that were rated from 3,883 rows in movies.dat.
Timestamp to datetime; confirm the May 2000 – January 2003 span.
Leakage scan: per-user first and last rating; cumulative ratings over time.

phases.title: Split design — before any feature is computed
points: Ttest at the 0.9 quantile of rating timestamps; Tval at the 0.8 quantile. A quantile, never a calendar date.
Protocol A — global temporal split. The real protocol.
Protocol B — per-user last-k. Leaks across users; what most published work does.
Protocol C — random k-fold. The ceiling of optimism.
Sensitivity across quantiles 0.8 / 0.85 / 0.9 / 0.95.
Cost accounting: users and films that survive A but not B.
Leakage assertions, including the count of training ratings that postdate a test rating under B — the leak, quantified.

phases.title: Distributional EDA (training window only)
points: Ratings per month; per-user active-span histogram; rating distribution and skew.
Long tails by film and by user; demographics coverage, zip in aggregate only.
Genre matrix, 18 binary columns.
Deliverable: a risk register and a preprocessing plan — not a folder of plots.

phases.title: Leakage-safe feature engineering
points: One control, applied uniformly: rolling, time-ordered cross-fitting. Random out-of-fold folds would reintroduce exactly what Phase 2 removed.
User and film history: count, mean, std, median, Q20, Q80 of prior ratings; recency.
Target-encoded means with smoothing toward the global mean, which handles cold users and films without a special case.
Content, static and context features carry no target and need no control.
Two feature views of the same statistics: one-hot for the linear rungs, target-encoded for the tree rungs.
Diagnostics with pass thresholds: permuted target (< 1% advantage), shuffled groups (no advantage), temporal boundary assertion.

phases.title: Baselines — the real opponent
points: Global mean, user mean, film mean.
Regularised bias model with its own tuned penalties — the opponent.
Computed under all three protocols; a baseline's value is protocol-specific.
Tuning budget declared before fitting, identical for the baseline and for the twelfth model.
The primary comparison and its three possible verdicts are written here, before any result is seen.

phases.title: The linear family
points: Simple, then multi-linear, then interactions, then polynomial count terms.
Centre continuous predictors; measure VIF before and after interacting, threshold 5.
Residuals vs fitted will show five diagonal bands — an artefact of a five-level target, not non-linearity.
The real diagnostic is shrinkage in predicted-vs-observed, and accepting it is a bias–variance decision.
A bounded ordinal cannot be log-transformed, so the usual heteroscedasticity remedy does not apply.
Count predictions outside [1,5]; report clipped and unclipped.

phases.title: Regularisation
points: Standardisation inside the fold — mandatory, since the penalty treats all coefficients alike.
Ridge and lasso over ~100 penalties, selected by the one-standard-error rule.
Stability selection over half-sample bootstraps: a selection frequency per feature.
Correlated groups flagged, with the member lasso happened to pick.
Train and validation error against complexity — the bias–variance figure as computable evidence.

phases.title: kNN regression
points: The prediction is stated first: at ~900k rows and 50+ features, kNN is outside its documented range on both axes. The phase tests that claim.
Distance treated as a tuned choice: Euclidean, Manhattan, Gower.
PCA first, then kNN — the documented remedy; accuracy and time reported.
Error against retained components, crossing the ~30–40 feature mark: the curse of dimensionality drawn from this project's own data.

phases.title: Trees
points: Continuous features win splits over binary ones by construction, so genre dummies will rarely be chosen.
Stopping conditions and cost-complexity pruning, alpha by time-aware CV; under 100 leaves for the readable version.
Permutation importance, never the default impurity measure.
Refit without the target-encoded means: what does the tree use when it is not handed the answer?
A tree cannot predict outside its training range.

phases.title: Ensembles
points: Bagging: variance reduction against the single tree, over repeated seeds.
OOB compared against the temporal validation, not against random CV; the gap is the finding.
Random Forest with subsample size and feature count declared, not defaulted.
Permutation importance tests the published 35% / 30% user-versus-film split rather than assuming it.
Gradient boosting with early stopping on the temporal validation set; staged error curve; residual fitting shown on one worked example.

phases.title: Stacking
points: Diversity measured first: the correlation matrix of out-of-fold predictions.
Out-of-fold predictions by time-ordered folds.
Non-negative ridge meta-learner, not ordinary least squares.
The weights are reported as a model-selection verdict: which rungs survived, which were zeroed.
Does the ensemble beat its best member, with intervals?

phases.title: Uncertainty and significance
points: Bootstrap clustered by user, not by row: ~100k test ratings come from at most 6,040 users.
Per-model intervals are descriptive and labelled “not a test”.
The primary comparison — best model against the regularised bias baseline — is paired, user-clustered, and pre-specified in Phase 4.
All other pairs form an exploratory family under Holm correction.
Coefficient tests for the unregularised model only; the post-selection limitation stated.
Prediction intervals, and seed spread kept separate from sampling uncertainty.

phases.title: Diagnostics
points: Every check here is exploratory and descriptive, declared in advance.
Leakage audit; calibration reliability diagram — predicted vs observed by decile.
Cold user and cold film, threshold declared with its reason plus sensitivity.
Error by rating value, read beside macro-MAEM.
Error by activity decile tested for a monotone trend.
Failure taxonomy: which kinds of rating are missed.
The optimism gap from four mechanisms: Protocol C, Protocol B, OOB, random k-fold.

phases.title: Report
points: Structured on the REFORMS checklist: leakage, evaluation design and uncertainty.
Reproducibility record: every seed, grid and budget, the data version, the environment, the wall-clock cost.
The pre-specified conclusion resolved, including the row that says the baseline was not beaten.
Model card; limitations stated plainly, including that these conclusions concern 6,040 users between 2000 and 2003.

baseline_note: A well-tuned simple baseline is hard to beat on dense rating data, and an under-tuned one makes the whole comparison an artefact of how the tuning budget was spent. So the bias model gets its own tuned penalties and the same budget as the twelfth model.
